correctness.rationale: For all finite girth-six-or-higher source graphs, unique connectors classify every noncore face as one of two maximal alternate-edge triangles per six-cycle. The full core is explicitly collapsed by free faces to the line-graph clique complex. Attaching loops represent the source hexagon, and the second disk is null after the first. Integral CW chain ranks give H2 free of rank 2h-r, H1 the exact cycle-lattice quotient. Tests enumerate full complexes and replay each proposed collapse but are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A uniform two-dimensional homotopy model for all high-girth line graph Rips complexes at the first nontrivial scale, admitting arbitrary overlaps of hexagons and computing the integral persistence kernel. It yields substantive nontrivial examples, including Heawood and subdivisions of complete graphs; neither core-only results nor disjoint-hexagon vertex-Rips classification gives this consequence.
